An analysis of the problem and the proposed solutions shows:

- A Fubini ranking corresponds to a standard competition ranking (ordered set partition $B_1 \mid B_2 \mid \dots \mid B_m$), where all competitors in block $B_j$ tie for rank $1 + \sum_{i < j} |B_i|$.
- Under the standard parking rule, each block $B_j$ occupies spots $\sum_{i < j} |B_i| + 1, \dots, \sum_{i \le j} |B_i|$ in increasing order of car labels. Thus, the resulting parking outcome $\pi$ is always the concatenation $\text{sort}(B_1) \cdot \text{sort}(B_2) \cdots \text{sort}(B_m)$.
- Since elements within each block must be strictly increasing, every descent in $\pi$ forces a block boundary. There are $k - 1$ descents and therefore $(n - 1) - (k - 1) = n - k$ ascents.
- At each of the $n - k$ ascents, one may independently choose whether or not to place a block boundary without affecting the resulting outcome $\pi$.
- This gives exactly $2^{n-k}$ valid Fubini rankings for any fixed outcome $\pi$ with $k$ ascending runs, as derived and verified in Solution 2.

CHOICE: 2
